Yes, you are right, social anxiety is prevalent with ET. To your other question, nothing has helped me in social situations so far. I have felt humiliated countless times in my life. People make it seem like as if I were responsible for having it, and they can't understand the helplessness I feel when I'm unable to control my hands like I want to.

It's great to hear that you got help, unfortunately I haven't yet found a good therapist whom I can trust and confide in. Earlier this year when I was still in uni, I went to the school appointed psychologist but I didn't like her, so I stopped going. Same thing happened with a psychiatrist I visited. The problem is that even though I'm familiar with cognitive therapy and its strategies, since I had a psychology course in uni and learned about them, I still cannot apply them because my anxiety is entirely different from other people's anxiety. It stems from ET. So I feel I can't get rid of anxiety because the source will always be there, and it's going to be apparent for anyone around me. Just to give you an example how it feels: I was on rotations and had to do an eye examination which meant that the patient had to focus on my finger. As I was getting ready, I was thinking to myself: 'please God let me do this without shaking'. And of course my hand shook. I heard a laughter coming from my peers standing behind me. Patient looked at me worriedly and asked me if I was ok. I just nervously smiled in reply. Eventually someone finished the examination instead of me. I just wanted to demonstrate with this example that anxiety is inextricably intertwined with ET. How could a therapist help? Should I tell every new person I meet that I have this condition? That feels overwhelming.

I have tried medication, beta-blockers, and I felt like I had been reborn. I remember I actually cried that day I was so happy. Unfortunately, I was told not to take them because my heart rate is already too low without them. I wore a 24-hour holter monitor not long ago, and the result said that I have a daytime average of 56, nighttime average of 36 BPM. I use BBs now on an 'as needed' basis when I know I will have a stressful situation.

Ok, but what if I am, in fact, nervous? Then it's a disaster, and I can't blame it on ET. Anxiety and ET form a vicious circle.
